overview: This single-page Department of State file list concerns Japan’s 1934 civil-aviation program. It records a confidential submission from Pan American Airways, Inc. reporting that Japan’s Ministry of Communications planned to extend airmail routes, train civilian pilots, improve aviation facilities, and increase the number of civilian aircraft while coordinating these measures with army and naval aviation.

subfiles.title: List of papers for “Post—Japan”
subfiles.about: A filing list describes confidential information submitted by Pan American Airways concerning Japan’s civil-aviation development program.
subfiles.summary: The sheet indexes a submission received on November 30, 1934, from Pan American Airways, Inc. It states that the Japanese Ministry of Communications’ program encompassed expanded airmail routes, civilian-pilot training, improved flying facilities, and more civilian aircraft. These initiatives were to be coordinated with army and naval aeronautics. The date 1945-10-17 appears to be the date or revision date of Department of State Form DS-46 rather than the underlying submission.

interest: Although only an index sheet survives here, it points to potentially significant confidential reporting on the close relationship between civil and military aviation in prewar Japan. The entry is useful for tracing how commercial aviation, pilot training, infrastructure development, and aircraft expansion were integrated with Japanese army and naval aeronautics as early as 1934. It also preserves provenance information for a Pan American Airways submission whose underlying memorandum is not included on this page.
